endorsements.quote: Developers must critically examine the fairness and diversity of the datasets they use.

Moreover, the medical AI community must prioritize the implementation of structural initiatives, such as standardized evaluations, fairness audits and transparent reporting, to ensure that AI systems perform equitably across diverse patient groups.
Agreed thresholds for acceptable performance disparities should be established to protect underserved populations from AI-induced harm.

Additionally, initiatives such as the STANDING Together project encourage systematic collection of demographic variables thus promoting inclusivity and diversity in health datasets ( Ganapathi et al., 2022 ).

unlisted_practices: Require early registration of AI models that influence clinical decisions, transparently disclosing training data, model performance, and processes governing deployment and updates.
Use federated learning and federated data access frameworks to enable cross-border, multi-institution model training while keeping patient data local.
Prioritize equitable representation among AI developers and researchers and build inclusive research cultures supporting scientists from marginalized and diverse socio-economic backgrounds.
Increase diversity of steering groups that develop AI reporting guidelines, particularly in gender and geographical representation.
Document transparently the entire AI model lifecycle, including development decisions, deployment environments, and post-deployment monitoring.
Collaborate with institutions in underrepresented regions such as Africa, Asia, and Latin America to integrate local health data into representative datasets.
Use public-private partnerships involving government bodies to promote transparency and accountability of AI in healthcare.

screen.reason: This is a brief report/commentary discussing the ethical imperatives, diversity, and governance frameworks (e.g., fairness audits, transparent AI development) necessary for responsible AI adoption in healthcare.
